notes:
Summary: evaluating Redwood Dedicated for low-latency trading assistant + high-throughput reranking pipelines. Primary concerns: guaranteed throughput under market peaks, predictable tail latency, and reserved GPU sizing for daily traffic plus 3x peak burst. 

Recent context: AE (Lena) + SE (Marco) ran an initial demo 2024-10-21 (see Fireflies). Cobalt Cortex completed questionnaire; security wants KMS/HSM integration and residency for PII. Procurement engaged but wants firm SLA language around p95/p99 latency and credit structure.

Customer voice (paraphrase): "We need predictable latency during market opens — can't have 500ms spikes. If you can't give throughput guarantees we go build internal autoscaler."

Key asks: reserved capacity plan for 8x A100-80GB equiv per region (primary + failover), warm pool sizing guidance, scale-up time targets (cold -> warm <30s), scale-down cooldowns (avoid thrashing), queueing/backpressure behavior when pools saturated, and credit terms for missed SLOs.

Triage notes: Marco to share perf trace from demo + queueing model spreadsheet. Legal asked for SLA draft; Redwood POC will run synthetic traffic simulating market-open pattern (100ms inter-arrival bursts). DevOps needs VPC peering checklist.

Callouts: cost-sensitive on per-token ELT pipeline; willing to trade quantization for cost if latency targets hold. Interested in Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching thresholds and KV cache hit-rate improvements.

throughput_targets: Sustained 350-500 QPS for reranking; burst up to 2,000 QPS for 30-120s windows during market events; embeddings backfill jobs off-peak (batch)
latency_slos: Target p50 <120ms, p95 <300ms, p99 <650ms for chat/re-ranking under normal traffic; strict tail constraints during bursts (p95 target enforced via reserved capacity). Will negotiate credit schedule for misses.
reserved_gpu_plan: Initial ask: reserve 8 x A100-80GB equiv in primary region + 2 x A100 warm standby; failover region reserve 4 x A100. Want guidance on effective vCPU/GPU ratio for preprocess workers. Open to Dedicated sizing proposal from Redwood.
sla_negotiation_points: Requests: 99.95% uptime, p95 latency SLOs per route, credit formula tied to observed p95 over monthly window, X_DR runbook for regional failover, security annex (KMS, audit logs). Legal wants sample SLO verbiage and historical latency percentiles.
autoscaling_requirements: Scale-up: prefer aggressive warm-pool expansion to handle 2x baseline bursts; target spin-up <30s for warm nodes, <90s for cold replacements. Scale-down: minimum warm-pool floor to avoid thrash (suggest 10% of baseline). Need hysteresis, cooldown 300s. Prefer policy examples: metric-based (queue depth + CPU/GPU utilization) combined with scheduled market-open ramp-up windows.
queueing_and_backpressure: When pools saturated, require predictable queueing behavior (max queue length, drop/retry semantics). Customer favors graceful degradation: route to lower-cost quantized model or degraded feature set before dropping requests. Wants observability: per-route queue depth, age, headway.
poc_plan: Run 3-day POC: day1 baseline perf, day2 simulated market open bursts (2k QPS), day3 failover and long-tail stress. Deliverables: latency percentiles, GPU utilization heatmaps, recommendation for warm-pool sizing and scale policies.

communication_preferences: Primary contact: infra-eng@cobaltcortex.ai (SLA comms via legal@cobaltcortex.ai). Prefers Slack for SE sync, email for legal/procurement.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Underprovisioned warm pools lead to tail latency spikes. Mitigation: conservative warm-pool floor + scheduled scale events around market opens. Risk: VPC peering delays. Mitigation: starter checklist and earlier engagement with network team.
sales_notes: High priority enterprise; champion in infra director (Eva Ren) pushing for vendor decision by end of Q1 FY25. Competitive tension: internal infra build vs Redwood Dedicated. Emphasize predictable economics and clear warm-pool playbook.
